message:
docs: record 0.2.128, and the four checks that could not have failed

Docs only. No product, test, or build file is touched, and the release source stays 9559368 --
this is the record, written after the freeze the way 0.2.127's was.

The docs stopped at the dispatcher measurement. Since then a reviewer found a real defect in the
preview budget, and I found several in my own work.

D1 is theirs and it mattered: thumb_busy and thumb_helper_lingering came back as Failed, so the
control session charged the window for a conflict between two dispatchers. Three of those and a
healthy window goes quiet for a minute -- the symptom this whole task exists to prevent, arriving
by a different road.

The rest are mine. Two paths where my tests reached into the user's machine: scratch hosts bound
the wildcard address because --bind-address defaults to INADDR_ANY, which raised firewall prompts
and left six Block rules; and udp_control_e2e_test defaulted at 127.0.0.1:43000, the installed
product, so a bare sweep sent hellos into the user's live session. Both causes are closed. That
nothing broke was luck, not design, and the docs say so.

A build that only worked here: a target registered with its source uncommitted, five commits that
a clean checkout could not configure. Worse than the mistake was the answer -- I said HEAD was fine
three times, having measured configure against my own working tree, which is not a clean checkout
and is exactly where the missing file was.

And four checks that would have passed no matter what: a gate marker the linker dropped, so linking
the fault file into the product still passed; a scanner with no positive control; a CMake check
that read the disk rather than the index; and a document check for control characters, added after
a heredoc wrote a vertical tab into a path. Every one was found by mutating the thing under test.
None would have been found by reading the green output.

What is still unproven is listed rather than rounded off: no installed build has been run, the
picker evidence is all isolated test binaries, the lingering branch has only been reached by
injection, six firewall rules remain, and a clean checkout needs the WebView2 SDK first.
